Subject: Runbook + links: Noah Reed — Tue Nov 10 10:30 PT (60m)

Team — final runbook and assignments for tomorrow’s coding screen. Please read quickly and add any callouts.

Slot: Tue Nov 10 — 10:30–11:30 PT (candidate confirmed)
Candidate: Noah Reed — resume attached, prefers Go
Location / platform: CoderPad session (live) — https://coderpad.io/p/8f3b2a
Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=Noah-Reed-coding-screen (I’ve sent invites to the panel)
Attachments (on thread): resume-noah-reed.pdf, screen-problem.md, coderpad-invite.txt

Agenda (60m):
- 0–5m: quick intros and context (Mina)
- 5–50m: paired coding (Jordan leads problem, Dev rotates in for design check-ins)
- 50–60m: private debrief (we'll use the Google Meet breakout + notes)

Evaluator assignments (primary):
- Jordan Blake: lead on implementation, guide candidate through the starter tests, assess code quality and debugging approach
- Dev Patel: focus on architecture decisions, edge cases, scaling considerations, and complexity trade-offs
- Laura Bennett: observe infra-related constraints (deployability, observability hooks, runtime costs) and timekeeper

Notes for pairing:
- Candidate will be allowed to run code but not look up complete solutions. We will give small hints if they get stuck.
- Problem is a medium system/algorithms mix — linked in screen-problem.md (attached).
- Use the CoderPad history to capture conversations; save a snapshot at the 45m mark for the debrief.

Debrief rubric (quick):
- Correctness (0–5)
- Problem decomposition / architecture (0–5)
- Code hygiene & tests (0–5)
- Communication & collaboration (0–5)
- Hire recommendation: Yes / Maybe / No (short justification)

Logistics:
- If anything shows up (conflict or tech issue), reply-all immediately and I’ll coordinate a fallback.
- I uploaded a pared-down problem and a short runner to the thread. If you want to practice the runner beforehand, open the CoderPad link and pick Go runtime.

Thanks — looking forward to this.
Mina
